Answer: B
Reason: The radiograph demonstrates Westermark sign (focal oligemia/hyperlucency) in the left upper lung zone and an elevated left hemidiaphragm, which are classic signs of acute pulmonary embolism without infarction caused by vascular obstruction and reflex diaphragmatic elevation. Hampton's hump (Option C) represents pulmonary infarction, which contradicts the "without infarction" constraint in the question.
